newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH 1996 BUDGET SHOWS CZK 3 BLN 11-MONTH DEFICIT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH 1996 BUDGET SHOWS CZK 3 BLN 11-MONTH DEFICIT.

text.p: The Czech 1996 state budget showed a three billion crown deficit for the first 11 months of the year, the local CTK agency said on Monday, quoting a finance ministry spokeswoman.
It said total expenditure was 434.4 billion crowns while revenue was 431.4 billion crowns for the 11-month period.
The result compares with a 1.2 billion crown surplus for through the first ten months of the year.
No reason was given for the swing into negative numbers, and finance ministry officials were not immediately available for further comment.
The 1996 budget draft was originally approved forecasting equal revenue and expenditure of about 497 billion crowns.
That was later revised to roughly 491 billion crowns, as budget cuts were made across the board to make up for an expected shortfall in revenue, and to keep the total in balance.
